account: The China Telecom Research Institute wrote the account of the Hui Xin assistant. The assistant interprets conversations with customers and retrieves information. It also fills in order forms. The institute lists DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), among its models. It reports that the assistant runs in two service halls as an initial phase. It reports that key process errors fell by over 50% and that marketing success rose by over 30%. It also reports that the assistant frees 20–30% of representatives’ time for other work. The account describes shorter waits for customers and broader accessibility, but it establishes no separate outcome for either. The institute plans to extend the assistant to 100 more halls.

comparator.after: The assistant fills order forms from the conversation; the developer reports that key process error rates fell by over 50% and that the average marketing success rate rose by over 30%.
comparator.against: Manual order entry by service representatives through the graphical interface of the business system
comparator.before: Representatives clicked through screens and typed customer details into order forms by hand.
comparator.quote: This GUI form-filling paradigm frees up 20%-30% of sales representatives' time for high-value tasks such as customer communication and marketing, cuts key process error rates by over 50%.
